html:
The rescue of the Bulgarian Jews was the halting of plans to deport the roughly 48,000 Jews of Bulgaria to the Nazi death camps in March 1943, after protests by politicians, the church and citizens.

Bulgaria was allied with Nazi Germany and had passed anti-Jewish laws. When trains were ready in March 1943, the deputy speaker of parliament Dimitar Peshev and 42 other deputies protested, and Metropolitans Stefan of Sofia and Kiril of Plovdiv spoke out. The deportations from Bulgaria itself were stopped. Yet the same government deported over 11,000 Jews from the lands it occupied in Yugoslav Macedonia and Greek Thrace, and almost all died at Treblinka. The story is a proud and painful part of how Bulgaria remembers the Holocaust.
sum: The rescue of the Bulgarian Jews was the halting of plans to deport the roughly 48,000 Jews of Bulgaria to the Nazi death camps in March 1943, after protests by politicians, the church and citizens.
